title: Israel Escalates Gaza Strikes, Warns Hamas Over Kite and Drone Launches
excerpt: Two airstrikes killed at least two people including a four-year-old boy on Sunday, as Israel threatened to intensify operations in Gaza over projectile launches despite the October 2025 ceasefire.
body:
• Israeli airstrikes in Gaza on Sunday killed at least two people, including a four-year-old boy, and wounded seven others
  • Israel warned Hamas it would intensify strikes and order civilian evacuations if launches of kites, balloons, and drones from Gaza did not stop
  • More than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect, according to Gaza health officials
  • Jared Kushner's meetings with both Israeli and Hamas leaders last week failed to produce a breakthrough on implementing Trump's Gaza roadmap

Sunday's Strikes

Two Israeli airstrikes hit the central Gaza Strip on Sunday, killing at least two people and wounding seven others, Palestinian health officials reported. One strike targeted a building in Zawayda, killing a four-year-old boy, Mohammad Abdel-Salam Taha, who died after being hit by flying debris and shrapnel. The second struck the nearby Nuseirat refugee camp.

Israel's military said it was looking into both incidents. The strikes followed the military's announcement late Saturday that it had killed Sharif Al-Hasnat, described as a senior Hamas militant in Deir Al-Balah who was leading efforts to restore Hamas's "underground infrastructure."

"There is no ceasefire, there is nothing. We want solutions, we want to live in peace."

— Abu Ahmed, displaced Palestinian near Zawayda

Kites as Justification

Following a situation assessment on Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office issued a warning to Hamas: stop launches of kites, balloons, and drones from Gaza toward Israel, or face intensified military operations and civilian evacuation orders.

The Israeli military has reported ongoing launches of incendiary and surveillance devices from Gaza, framing them as security threats that justify continued operations. Critics, including Al Jazeera reporting, have characterized Israel's use of kite and balloon launches as a pretext to justify escalating strikes that have continued despite the ceasefire agreement.

The October 2025 U.S.-backed ceasefire was meant to halt major fighting in the territory, but has failed to stop Israeli military operations. According to Gaza health officials, more than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire took effect, while the Israeli military reports four soldiers killed in the same period.

Kushner Diplomacy Stalls

The strikes came days after Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's son-in-law and senior adviser, left Jerusalem without securing a breakthrough on the broader Gaza roadmap. Kushner met Netanyahu and then traveled to Egypt to meet mediators and Hamas leaders.

An official from Trump's Board of Peace said Israel retained its "full right of self-defense" and that there would be no military "redeployment" until Hamas was disarmed. Netanyahu made clear the military would continue operating in Gaza with no troop pullback.

Hamas accuses Israel of violating the ceasefire and undermining Trump's plan, which envisions Israeli withdrawals alongside Hamas disarmament. A Palestinian observer in Egypt, speaking anonymously, said Hamas leaders "do not believe in an agreement with the current Israeli government."

Expanding Occupation

Since the ceasefire began, Israel has expanded its occupation to control approximately 70 percent of Palestinian territory in Gaza, according to Le Monde reporting. Humanitarian organizations continue to denounce obstacles to aid delivery.

Egypt, a key mediator, has expressed urgency about moving the process forward. "The current situation can only lead to more friction and pressure on Palestinian civilians and, unfortunately, an expansion of Israeli security zones and occupation," said Nabil Fahmy, Egyptian diplomat and secretary general of the Arab League.

One of the core sticking points remains Israel's broad interpretation of "imminent threat" — a concept it uses to justify strikes on Gaza. Kushner and Netanyahu agreed to establish a "deconfliction mechanism" involving Egyptian mediators, though no details were provided.

West Bank Violence

Violence also flared in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Sunday. An Israeli man was stabbed and wounded near Jericho by a suspected Palestinian attacker who fled the scene. Separately, Israeli forces shot and killed a 14-year-old boy, Islam Ajjouri, during a raid into Askar refugee camp near Nablus, according to Palestinian health officials. The Israeli military said it was investigating the incident.
